
### (de)multiplexing 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-demultiplexing.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Diagram showing two flows (on between machines 1 and 2; the other between machines 3 and 4), each divided up into packets. The flows both pass from the source machine, to a first switch, then to a second switch, then to the destination machine. Packets from both flows are interleaved on the link connnecting the two switches and some packets wait in queues on each of the switches."}

![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-demultiplexing.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Same diagram with the link connecting the two switches highlighted. That link has some packets from each flow in transit on it."}

![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-demultiplexing.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Same diagram with the two switches highlighted."}

![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-demultiplexing.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt=""}

![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-demultiplexing.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="Same diagram with queues on each switch highlighted. Switch 1 has a queue of packets from both flows in front of the shared link. Switch 2 has two separate queues, one in front of its link to machine 2 and the other in front of its link to machine 4. In each of these queues, packets from exactly one flow wait."}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=2 .fade-in-then-out}

two or more flows can share one or more links

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=3 .fade-in-then-out}

left switch _multiplexes_ the two flows onto one link <br/>
<br/>
right switch _demultiplexes_ them to separate them

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=4 .fade-in-then-out}

this picture: multiplexed by dividing up _time_ on link

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment fragment-index=5 .fade-in-then-out}

switches usually have _buffers_ (also called _queues_)<br/>
holds waiting packets

:::



### bursts and dropping 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-bursts-and-dropping.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Same diagram as previous slide, but with the buffers highlighted."}

![](/intro/texfig/muxdemux-bursts-and-dropping.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Same diagram as previous slide, but the queue on the right switch (before the shared link) is overflowing with packets."}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment framgment-index=1 .fade-in-then-out}

switch absorb "bursts" of packets<br/>
would be basically empty if we could send packets immediately

:::


::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment framgment-index=2 .fade-in-then-out}

incomplete list of causes of bursts:<br/>
multiple unsynchronized flows <br/>
fast links produce packets faster than slow can send

:::

::: {.myoverbox .low .fragment framgment-index=3 .fade-in-then-out}

if buffer full, switch must _drop_ packets<br/>
called _congestion<br/>
<br/>
will happen eventually if overall rate faster than link

:::
